column1: # Dietary marks, transcribed from the printed menus on 2026-08-22:
# Both venues print the same key:
#   V vegetarian · VG vegan · GF gluten free · GFA gluten free available
#   DF dairy free · N contains nuts · A australian · I imported
# A and I are PROVENANCE, not dietary, and are deliberately not imported.
# `printed` is exactly what the menu shows — the audit trail.
# `apply`   is what gets written to Recipe.dietary. Where the two differ,
# An empty `apply` claims NOTHING, which the register reads as "nobody has
# checked" rather than "safe". That is the whole safety model: a dish can be
# ruled OUT on a contains tag, never ruled IN by the absence of one.

column8: shellfish is not on the printed key, but shrimp is shellfish. A contains tag can only rule a dish OUT, so adding it can only make the filter safer.
